object_description: four raised wings arranged around a central circulation ring
design_condition: Four buildings are raised above the flood level around a central ring, but their disconnection from the ground and schematic landscape integration weaken the relationship with the site.

positive.statement: The cells distributed along two facades offer a diversity of views and orientations.

position.rationale: Repeated cell modules are visible along opposing linear wings in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The three wings housing the six divisions have a fairly clear organization.

position.rationale: The wing arrangement and repeated divisions are clearly legible in the top view.

positive.statement: The structural, technical-distribution, and sustainability responses are adequate.

position.rationale: This evaluates non-spatial building systems rather than a locatable geometric feature.

positive.statement: The phasing is well designed, with small contact surfaces facilitating realization of the second phase.

position.target: small contact surfaces for the second phase
position.rationale: A peripheral wing junction provides a plausible location for phased contact and construction.

positive.statement: The project author plans areas for later expansion.

position.rationale: Outer wing ends offer plausible expansion zones within the dispersed composition.

negative.statement: The small patios raise questions about their real usefulness and compliance with regulations.

position.rationale: Small enclosed voids are visible beside the central ring and wing edges.

negative.statement: The great depth of the lower floors greatly reduces natural light in the workshops.

position.rationale: Deep linear floor plates are visible in plan, with lower levels constrained by elevations.

negative.statement: Raising the buildings solves flooding but leaves them disconnected from the ground, while the stairs and ramps are not integrated into the architecture.

position.rationale: Raised linear masses and access appendages are visible around the central circulation ring.

negative.statement: The residual arrangement of buildings and promenades does not provide the privacy required for security.

position.rationale: Peripheral gaps between wings and circulation strips provide the site-level privacy concern.

negative.statement: The project does not convincingly integrate into the landscape, which remains very schematic.

position.rationale: The outer ground-facing perimeter is the plausible location for schematic landscape treatment.

negative.statement: The mix of functions in the central building raises questions about the establishment’s functioning.

position.rationale: The central ring and adjoining compact volume are clearly identifiable in plan.

negative.statement: Access from the distant divisions requires crossing other divisions, creating problematic circulation.

position.rationale: The outer wing-to-center route is inferred from the separated linear divisions.

negative.statement: The high-security division is too exposed to contact with other prisoners and people outside the establishment.

position.rationale: A peripheral wing zone is used as the constrained location for the unspecified secure division.

negative.statement: Logistical circulation creates risks of contact between prisoners and external people across the site.

position.rationale: The lower site edge and inter-wing routes are the plausible logistical circulation surface.

negative.statement: The great building depth creates problems for horizontal evacuation routes.

position.rationale: Deep horizontal wings provide the constrained floor-level evacuation location.

negative.statement: The second-degree evolution of the concept is unconvincing and introduces functionality issues that were previously absent.

position.rationale: The judgment concerns the later overall arrangement, anchored to the dispersed wing composition.

negative.statement: The proposed expansion areas are not shown to work as a coherent whole.

position.rationale: Peripheral open-ended wing areas plausibly represent the proposed expansion zones.
